capabilities.target: payments-agent pay_vendor skill, ultimately a vendor bank account

inputs.source: Vendor quote emails and attachments from external senders

instructions.note: The prompt states payments-agent will handle remaining checks, but runtime notes show payments-agent performs no verification and pays the bank details in the task, trusting any task on the orchestrator's bearer token. The orchestrator is effectively relying on a safety control that does not exist downstream.
"Choose the best one" gives no objective criteria for selecting among quotes, leaving the decision open to influence by content in untrusted vendor quote emails.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: A genuine human decision gates creation of the purchase request, but it occurs before any vendor quote exists and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent, so it does not gate the vendor selection or bank-detail destination that cap.delegate_payment actually carries.

controls.name: Prompt instruction restricting payment to approved vendor list
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced only by the model following prompt.md line 3. The check is on vendor name/identity, not on verified bank account details, so a fraudulent or compromised quote purporting to be from an approved vendor can still carry attacker bank details that the model accepts, and a more capable model can rationalize more convincing exceptions.

controls.name: Destination/recipient confirmation bound to vendor system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Would make the payment destination independent of whatever bank details appear in an inbound quote email, closing the business email compromise path regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Signed and pinned payments-agent card
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; the agent card is fetched at startup without signature verification or pinning per the runtime notes, allowing undetected redefinition or impersonation of payments-agent.

controls.name: Mutual authentication for the A2A channel to payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; only a static bearer token scheme is declared, which payments-agent accepts for any task per the runtime notes.

findings.title: Authority laundering enables business email compromise payment fraud (TC7)

attack_path.note: Untrusted external vendor quote email supplies vendor identity and bank details
Manager approval was already granted for item/budget only, before any quote existed; the approval record is not passed forward
Agent checks vendor identity against the approved list, a name-level check only
Agent delegates a payment task, including bank details taken from the quote, to payments-agent over A2A
payments-agent trusts any task bearing the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task without further verification

forecast.watch_signal: A model version change on procurement-orchestrator, an increase in autonomy or unattended runtime, or removal/loosening of the vendor allowlist instruction without adding a structural destination confirmation.

evidence.observation: Manager approves item/budget before any quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.

Agent is instructed to choose the best vendor quote, use bank details from the chosen quote, restrict to the approved list, and rely on payments-agent for remaining checks that runtime notes show do not exist.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company, an untrusted channel.

recommendations.action: Bind the payment destination account to a verified system-of-record value captured at vendor onboarding, out of band from quote emails; have payments-agent reject or hold for review any delegate_payment call whose bank details do not match that record, independent of model judgment.

Propagate the manager's approval context, including the finally selected vendor and bank details, to payments-agent, and require payments-agent to validate the payment against that specific approved context rather than trusting any task on the shared bearer token.
Add reconciliation or anomaly detection comparing payment bank details against the vendor record before funds are released, and alert on mismatch.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card with static bearer auth allows agent impersonation and rug pull (ASI04/ASI07)

attack_path.note: Agent card fetched at startup over an unverified channel; not signed, hashed, or pinned
Orchestrator delegates payment authority and bearer-token trust to whatever endpoint answers as payments-agent

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

evidence.observation: Authentication schemes are limited to bearer; the card carries no signature or pinning information.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.

recommendations.action: Pin or hash the payments-agent card and verify its signature on every fetch; fail closed on mismatch.
Replace the shared static bearer token with mutually authenticated, per-task scoped credentials (mTLS or signed identity) between procurement-orchestrator and payments-agent.
Log and alert on any change to the payments-agent card or endpoint, and on authentication anomalies on the A2A channel.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach an S3 sink (irreversible delegated payment carrying confidential bank details) from an untrusted or unverified source. On the authority-laundering path the only credited control is a dependent, behavioral vendor-name check, since the one human approval in the design precedes vendor selection and its record is never passed to payments-agent, so it earns no credit against this capability; that yields a residual of high. On the agent-identity path there is no credited control at all: the agent card is unsigned and unpinned and the A2A channel relies on a static bearer token payments-agent accepts for any task, leaving residual at critical. The overall residual is therefore critical. Forecast stays critical because the one control earning credit (the vendor allowlist instruction) is dependent and is expected to fail under model upgrade, longer task horizons, or increased autonomy, and the identity-gap path has no control to lose in the first place.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, payments-agent agent card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior; actual production behavior may differ.

No MCP/A2A traffic capture, IaC, or source code was provided; the exact credential scope and validation logic inside payments-agent are inferred from the runtime notes rather than verified configuration, which is why credential_scope and auth_method are recorded with medium-to-high confidence rather than verified status.

No schema for the manager approval record was provided; whether any version of that approval could technically include vendor or bank-detail fields is inferred solely from the stated sequencing, that approval happens before quotes exist.
